schema_invariants: Every durable identity is a bounded nonempty string with an explicit uniqueness scope.
Every mutable resource has a positive monotonic revision and immutable prior revisions or tombstones.
Every canonical typed value, catalog, dictionary, container, namespace, and file record carries a SHA-256 content digest.
Every foreign key is explicit and deletion is restricted or tombstoned rather than implicitly cascading authoritative history.
Every enum and Boolean domain is constrained equivalently in SQLite and PostgreSQL.
Every timestamp is authoritative database UTC time and never supplied by a browser.
Idempotency and audit-outbox uniqueness prevents duplicate settlement under concurrent retries.

schema_fingerprint_record.canonicalization: ordered table, column, type, nullability, default, primary-key, foreign-key, unique, check, and index definitions with backend-equivalent domains normalized by the migration code
schema_fingerprint_record.persistence_rule: 0007 writes its own immutable fingerprint row and does not add, remove, or alter any column or accepted row in the v0.7 schema_migrations table
schema_fingerprint_record.startup_rule: data-service mutations remain disabled unless the recomputed backend schema fingerprint exactly matches the persisted 0007 record

backend_parity.canonical_semantics: identical schema constraints, transaction outcomes, ordering, digest bytes, revisions, and error classifications
backend_parity.sqlite: foreign keys enabled, bounded busy timeout, WAL concurrency policy, and explicit immediate write transactions
backend_parity.postgresql: serializable or row-locked compare-and-set for conflicting mutations with bounded retry classification

migration_transaction.preflight: verify predecessor, schema fingerprint, absence of unexpected objects, and backup destination before DDL
migration_transaction.application: one transactional migration where supported; SQLite rebuild steps use an explicit rollback-safe transaction
migration_transaction.postflight: verify exact object inventory, constraints, indexes, schema fingerprint, and predecessor record digests
migration_transaction.failure: roll back all new objects and leave 0007 pending
migration_transaction.idempotency: reapplying a recorded migration verifies the same schema fingerprint and performs no mutation

backup_contents: virtual-file metadata and exact content bytes
backup_restore.consistency: database snapshot and virtual-file content are captured at one quiesced revision boundary
backup_restore.restore_rule: restore into an empty isolated target and verify every digest and schema invariant before a separate explicit activation decision
backup_restore.sqlite_activation: while the service is stopped, manually replace the configured database file only after exact isolated-target verification and retain the prior file for rollback
backup_restore.postgresql_activation: reconstruct and verify a separately named isolated database; this contract does not authorize database rename, connection swap, replication, online cutover, or automatic activation

corruption_matrix.target: typed value, catalog, dictionary, container, or namespace digest
backup manifest, member inventory, or aggregate digest

rollback_policy.empty_unactivated_v08_schema: may remove exactly the fifteen v0.8 tables only when data_schema_fingerprints contains exactly the matching 0007 record with activated false; every other v0.8 table has zero rows; no v0.8 virtual-file content, idempotency settlement, audit-outbox event, unknown object, or later migration exists; and the live schema fingerprint exactly matches 0007
rollback_policy.populated_schema: restore the verified pre-migration backup; destructive down-migration is forbidden
rollback_policy.rollback_success_claim: requires restored schema and record digests equal to the pre-migration manifest

restart_recovery: A crash before migration commit leaves 0007 pending and no visible partial schema.
A crash after commit resumes from the recorded schema fingerprint without replaying DDL.
A crash during backup leaves an uncommitted temporary backup that is never eligible for restore.
A crash during restore leaves the active target unchanged until full validation and activation complete.
Data services remain mutation-disabled whenever schema, record, content, or evidence verification fails.
